chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Kazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Jabir ibn Abd Allah: 'O Jabir, this is the month of Ramadan. Whoever fasts its day, prays during a portion of its night, keeps his stomach and private parts chaste, and restrains his tongue, will emerge from his sins as he emerged from the month.' Jabir said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful is this hadith!' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O Jabir, how severe are these conditions!'

key_terms.عَفَّ بَطْنُهُ وَ فَرْجُهُ: Kept his stomach and private parts chaste
key_terms.قَامَ وِرْدًا: Prayed during a portion/part of the night

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions for complete forgiveness of sins during Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* emphasizes that Ramadan serves as a comprehensive expiation for sins, contingent upon a holistic discipline of the body, speech, and devotion. The Prophet’s rhetorical question regarding the severity of these conditions underscores the rigorous spiritual standard required to attain this divine mercy, a theme central to Shia ethical teachings on self-purification (*tazkiyah*).
